criteria_scores.rationale: Strong fit to a confined acid-water / hybrid hopping mechanism: the ChCl/PA eutectic directly supports acid complexation and reduced crystallisation tendency, while starch/PVA supplies dense OH-rich hydrogen-bond relays.

Moderate-to-good conductivity is plausible from the DES-like proton carrier plus OH-rich matrix, but direct quantitative evidence for this exact membrane architecture is limited and most anchors are indirect.

Scores well for the 182–299 K window because (a) it has an explicit anti-freeze / eutectic strategy, (b) starch/PVA is a plasticised low-temperature-capable host rather than a brittle HT-PEM matrix, and (c) the acid is complexed rather than neat free PA. For (d), the descriptor pool supports the ChCl/PA eutectic motif, but quantitative conductivity anchors are mainly above room temperature; therefore this is strong but not maximal.

Retention is plausible through hydrogen bonding and eutectic complexation, but humidity-cycling retention versus acid leaching is not directly demonstrated for this exact starch/PVA-ChCl/PA combination.
All components are compatible with solution blending / casting and do not imply demanding thermal processing.

Independent D4 audit is strong: all declared (component, descriptor) pairs are backed in the upstream pool with direct matches for starch D5/D6, PVA D6, ChCl D4, and PA D4; only PA D6 is analog-indirect rather than exact, so support remains high.
Main risks are over-softening from eutectic loading and uncertain long-term retention under humidity cycling, but no obvious show-stopper is evident.
Shares the phosphoric-acid family logic and low-temperature target, but replaces the clay-centered S8 mother system with an eutectic/polymer route.
Typical university-lab feasible: commodity reagents, likely solution processing, no glove box implied.
Starch is biomass-derived and widely available; the rest are common chemicals.

novel_combination: closest support is the ChCl/PA eutectic paper manual_1ca1249fc4, but that does not report this starch/PVA membrane integration; the transfer into an OH-rich film for cold-window operation is the differentiating step.

ranked_candidates.ranking_rationale: Ranked first because its combination_novelty is high as a true novel_combination, and it is one of the strongest candidates on cold_to_room_T_robustness due to the explicit ChCl/PA eutectic anti-freeze strategy. It also scores very well on experimental_feasibility, making the novelty-versus-feasibility balance attractive even though S8 proximity is only moderate.
ranked_candidates.novelty_rationale: The novelty is the transfer of a ChCl/PA eutectic motif into a starch/PVA OH-rich film aimed at subambient continuity. Evidence supports each role individually, but this exact combined membrane was not directly claimed in the pool.
ranked_candidates.risk_summary: Good low-temperature concept and easy processing, but film over-softening and acid retention under humidity cycling remain the main development risks.

criteria_scores.rationale: Very strong match to the winning mechanism: attapulgite offers 1-D confinement, chitosan/PVA provide dense hydrogen-bonded relay media, and PA is the proton source for hybrid hopping in confined domains.

Component analogs suggest meaningful conductivity is achievable, especially given the attapulgite/chitosan precedent and PA-mediated transport; however, the exact quaternary blend lacks direct low-temperature performance proof.

Moderately good for 182–299 K: (a) OH-rich hydrated film plausibly preserves bound-water continuity, but there is no explicit anti-freeze co-solvent; (b) polymer blend continuity should be better than brittle HT-PEM hosts; (c) free PA has only partial mitigation via clay/polymer interactions, so acid cold-stability is intermediate; (d) there is a PA quantitative anchor at −30 °C in the pool, but not for this exact chemistry. Hence a solid but not top-tier low-T score.
Chitosan-clay interactions and attapulgite confinement provide a credible route to suppress PA loss relative to unconfined acid-doped films.
Likely accessible by aqueous or mixed-solvent casting with conventional blending and filler dispersion.

Independent D4 audit is good: chitosan D5/D7, attapulgite D5/D7, and PVA D6 are backed directly in the pool. PA D4 is directly backed, while PA D6 is analog-backed via H3PO4/PA variants and related low-temperature PA literature, so overall coverage is strong but not perfect.
Risks are mainly balancing enough PA for conductivity without excessive plasticisation or leaching, plus the lack of direct subzero data for the exact quaternary formulation.
This is a minimal perturbation of the phosphoric-acid-in-clay S8 family, adding film-forming biopolymers around a clay-confined acid motif.
Uses commodity polymers, clay filler, and phosphoric acid; standard membrane casting and drying should suffice.
Chitosan is biomass-derived and broadly accessible; other components are also common.

novel_combination: closest support is the chitosan/1-D attapulgite proton-transport literature around manual_1190463586 and related chitosan-attapulgite work, but the exact CS/PVA/attapulgite/PA cold-targeted quaternary film is not directly reported.

ranked_candidates.ranking_rationale: This candidate ranks near the top because its combination_novelty is high and its mechanism consistency is among the best in the set. Its cold_to_room_T_robustness is good but lower than the eutectic-based design because it lacks an explicit anti-freeze co-solvent. It remains highly attractive thanks to strong s8_proximity and excellent experimental_feasibility.
ranked_candidates.novelty_rationale: This is the requested quaternary synergy motif assembled from separately supported roles rather than a directly reported exact formulation. Novelty lies in combining biopolymer retention, PVA film flexibility, 1-D clay confinement, and phosphoric-acid conduction in one cold-targeted membrane.
ranked_candidates.risk_summary: Mechanistically strong and close to the S8 family, but low-temperature continuity is still inferential and free-PA overloading could cause softness or leaching.

criteria_scores.rationale: Very good match to the confined acid-water hybrid-hopping mechanism: HNTs provide direct confinement and chitosan adds acid-interacting retention and hydrated transport continuity.
Reasonable conductivity is plausible from HNT-confined PA plus a chitosan host, but there is no direct quantitative anchor for this exact ternary membrane in the target temperature window.

Moderate score for the 182–299 K window: (a) hydrated chitosan can support bound-water continuity but no explicit anti-freeze additive is present; (b) the matrix is softer than HT-PEM controls; (c) PA is only partially stabilised by confinement and polymer interaction; (d) low-temperature PA-related analog evidence exists in the pool, but not for this exact HNT/chitosan system.
Retention should be relatively strong because both HNT confinement and chitosan acid interaction work in the same direction against leaching.
Composite membrane casting is straightforward, though HNT dispersion control matters.
Independent D4 audit is very strong: chitosan D5/D7, HNT D5/D7, and PA D4/D6 all have direct or near-direct upstream backing, with little unsupported descriptor inflation.
Primary risks are HNT aggregation and the absence of direct subzero conductivity validation, but the concept is otherwise coherent.
Still very close to the phosphoric-acid-in-clay S8 family, differing mainly by use of HNTs and a chitosan binder/scaffold.
No unusual equipment implied; standard dispersion and casting methods should be sufficient.
Chitosan is biomass-derived and widely accessible.
novel_combination: closest paper is the PA@HNT motif in manual_a16330d0f5, but embedding that motif into a chitosan retention scaffold is the new combination-level step.

ranked_candidates.ranking_rationale: This candidate is ranked highly because its combination_novelty is strong while remaining closely tied to an already validated PA@HNT confinement motif. Its cold_to_room_T_robustness is only moderate since it lacks an explicit anti-freeze strategy, but that is partly offset by high evidence_support and excellent experimental_feasibility.
ranked_candidates.novelty_rationale: This candidate extends the proven PA@HNT confinement motif by embedding it in a chitosan retention scaffold. The combination is novel relative to the pool but built from directly compatible component-level claims.
ranked_candidates.risk_summary: Good retention logic and strong audit support, with main risks centered on nanotube dispersion and unproven subzero transport.

criteria_scores.rationale: Directly consistent with the mechanism through acid confinement in nanotubular clay and dense hydrogen-bonded PA domains.
Good intrinsic conductivity potential is supported by the PA@HNT literature, though the architecture is less complete as a stand-alone membrane system.

Confinement may help the cold end, but this is still mostly a free-PA/clay motif without an explicit anti-freeze co-solvent or soft polymer host. There is no direct 182–299 K quantitative anchor for this specific motif, so the low-temperature robustness is capped at a middling level.
One of the strongest features: HNT confinement is directly supported as reducing PA leaching.
As supplied, this is better viewed as a confined-acid additive or powder motif than a complete membrane, so processability into a robust free-standing film is less straightforward.
Independent D4 audit is strong with direct upstream support for HNT D5/D7 and PA D4/D6 via the pool.
Main risk is practical: brittle compact / powder handling and likely need for a binder or matrix for real membrane deployment.
Extremely close to the phosphoric-acid-in-clay mother system.
Impregnation/loading is feasible, but forming a practical membrane typically needs an added support or binder.
Neutral default for a non-biomass route.
exact_match: this is intentionally a control baseline, closest to manual_a16330d0f5 and directly represented in the pool, so novelty is explicitly penalised.

ranked_candidates.ranking_rationale: This exact_match control stays in the list because it is mechanistically relevant and experimentally grounded, but it does not out-rank the better argued novel combinations. ranked_candidates.novelty_rationale: This is retained as a control because the PA@HNT motif is directly represented by the claim pool. It anchors the candidate set with one low-novelty benchmark for confined-acid transport.
ranked_candidates.risk_summary: Useful as a benchmark confined-acid control, but likely needs a binder/matrix and is not the most persuasive low-temperature membrane on its own.

criteria_scores.rationale: Partially aligned: the amorphous phosphate glass can provide proton-conducting domains, but this is less clearly a confined acid-water network than the clay/PA or eutectic candidates.

Phosphate glass has real proton-conducting precedent, but the integrated polymer/glass interfacial pathway quality is uncertain and the component literature is not targeted to the exact cold hydrated regime.

This scores low for the 182–299 K window: there is no explicit anti-freeze/bound-water mitigation, glassy domains may not ensure mechanical/electrical continuity at 200 K, and the literature anchors are predominantly high-temperature or condition-unspecified. Because the support is closer to HT proton-conducting archetypes than explicit cold-end operation, the score is capped low.
The inorganic phase may help immobilise protonic species, but stability is reported as condition-dependent and interface-driven failure is plausible.
Hybridising a brittle inorganic glass with soft biopolymers is feasible but less straightforward than simple solution-cast polymer/clay systems.
Independent D4 audit is excellent: all claimed descriptor pairs for phosphate glass, starch, and PVA are directly represented in the upstream claim pool.
Interfacial brittleness, unclear low-temperature continuity, and condition-sensitive conductivity stability are meaningful risks.
It shares proton-conduction descriptors but moves well away from the phosphoric-acid-in-clay mother family.
Still lab-accessible, but preparing and integrating protonated phosphate glass is a moderate barrier compared with commodity aqueous casting.
Starch is widely available, with PVA also common.

novel_combination: closest support is the phosphate-glass literature manual_26f0dcfc01/manual_3d7d6d5d7b plus starch/PVA support, but the cold-oriented glass/starch/PVA hybrid membrane itself is not directly reported.

ranked_candidates.ranking_rationale: The candidate is novel at the combination level and very well supported by the independent descriptor audit, but its cold_to_room_T_robustness is clearly weaker than the top polymer/clay or eutectic designs because its anchors are mainly outside the explicit 182–299 K target regime. ranked_candidates.risk_summary: Interesting high-novelty hybrid, but glass/polymer compatibility and weak direct low-temperature support make it a riskier cold-window candidate.

ranking_notes: All candidates were retained because each has a non-empty novelty_rationale, but X1/X2/X3 are obvious off-topic distractors and therefore rank at the bottom on mechanism consistency, cold-to-room-temperature robustness, and S8 proximity. Evidence-support scoring used the upstream descriptor_claim_pool (D4 audit) rather than self-reported claims. For several candidates, literature anchors inside the explicit 182–299 K window are sparse; where only elevated-temperature or condition-unspecified component analogs exist, cold_to_room_T_robustness was capped accordingly.
